member.summary: Serves user-uploaded avatars from the local upload store through a token-gated route (Milestone 4.1, ADR 0013 §2.4) — the free stand-in for a Blob SAS. It is because the signed t token IS the capability (like a SAS), not the auth cookie: public title-detail pages render reviewer avatars anonymously. member.name: T:Cinora.Web.Infrastructure.PwaCacheControlMiddleware
member.summary:
Sets Cinora's deliberate PWA cache policy on HTML responses so the service worker (Milestone 6.1, ADR 0019) caches exactly the right pages:
Authenticated HTML → Cache-Control: no-store (private). The SW refuses to cache a no-store response, so one user's personalized pages (/home feed, /notifications, /settings, /friends, /watchlist) are never stored in the shared SW cache where a second user on a shared device could read them offline.
Anonymous public GET HTML → Cache-Control: no-cache (cacheable, revalidate). The framework stamps no-cache, no-store on every token-rendering page (ASP.NET Core anti-forgery calls SetDoNotCacheHeaders whenever the layout renders the token). Left as-is, the SW could never cache a public page and offline browsing would be impossible. This relaxes that blanket to no-cache — never no-store — so the SW may cache the landing / /discover / Details / search pages for offline reading, while shared and HTTP caches still revalidate (no page is served stale without a round-trip). CSRF is unaffected: the double-submit token↔cookie check runs on POST, not on caching.
/offline → Cache-Control: no-cache always (the SW precaches it; it must never be marked no-store even for an authenticated viewer, or offline browsing loses its fallback).
member.remarks: The header is decided from a callback so the response Content-Type and the authenticated principal are both known, and so it wins over the anti-forgery header set during view rendering. Registered after UseAuthentication/UseAuthorization so HttpContext.User is populated; static files are served upstream by UseStaticFiles, so their long-lived immutable caching is never touched here. Anonymous non-GET responses (e.g. a failed login re-render) keep the framework's no-store intact.

member.name: T:Cinora.Web.ViewModels.Common.AvatarViewModel
member.summary: The model for the shared _Avatar partial (§3, §11): everything the seam needs to render a real avatar (via IFileStorage.GetUrl) or the monogram fallback is just the owner's and . Designed so any surface that shows a user (profile, review card, feed item, comment) can drop the partial in with only those two values plus a size. The partial — never the caller — decides whether the key is safe to sign into a URL, so a corrupt key degrades to the monogram rather than throwing (ADR 0013 §2.4; architecture L3).
member.param: The user's display name (drives the monogram initial and the image alt text).
The user's avatar storage key, or null to render the monogram.
The render size preset; defaults to .

When true, the avatar is rendered as a DECORATIVE image (empty alt / aria-hidden monogram) so a screen reader does not double-announce the name — use this on every surface where a VISIBLE adjacent name (a review/comment/feed/friend card's name link, the profile header, the notification message) already conveys the user. Defaults to false (the accessibility-safe default: a MEANINGFUL alt / labelled monogram), which is correct wherever the avatar stands alone with no adjacent visible name — e.g. the nav chip.

When true, the avatar loads with loading="eager" instead of the default lazy (Milestone 6.4 §6.5, backlog 4.2 Low). Use it for ABOVE-THE-FOLD placements — the nav chip and the profile/settings header — so the image is not deferred and does not paint late; the reserved box means there is no CLS either way. Defaults to false (lazy) for everything below the fold (cards, lists, feed rows).
